title: A backup's record
description: The backup.json in each backup's folder (Game runtimes, Backups): the save the backup holds and each of its files, so a restore or an export can check the files before it uses them. A game runtime writes it with each backup it takes, and vhd import writes it, through the game runtime's image, for a save it takes. It is written whole and synced before its folder takes a backup's name, so a folder named as a backup always has one. A reader takes only the keys it needs, so a key a later release adds does not break it; a record from before this contract has no source, and counts as the runtime's.

world.description: The world's save name. A restore refuses a backup of another world.

save.description: The save's number, from its _main.<n>.ok (Game facts). Numbers wrap and repeat.

written_ns.description: When the game completed the save: its .ok's modification time, in nanoseconds of Unix time. With the number, it names the save a backup holds, so a runtime never backs the same save up twice.

objects.description: The objects the save holds, as its .chunks file counts them. World truth judges a restored save against it.

taken.description: When the backup was taken, in UTC: the time its folder is named for.

source.description: Where the backup came from. runtime: the world's game runtime took it from the world's save. import: vhd import took it from a save the server manager put in the install folder. Absent in a record from before this contract, which counts as runtime.

files.description: Every file of the save, each once: the save's own four and its chunks, named as in the world's save folder. A restore copies exactly these and checks each one's size and SHA-256.
